name: define: inputs arrive on inputs and run the code at the frame's end
inputs set at the placing wait for the first read, then arrive in order
this is kept and counts the runs: once a frame however many arrivals, and the same value again runs it
the run's third argument names the inputs that arrived since the last run
a signal input calls the function of its name once a frame; a signal output is a function on outputs
a signal before the first read is held and heard after it
setup when read, destroy when the code is replaced, and this across both — the same code set again is read again
because: javascript.ts :307-314 (destroy, then read), :416-428 (setup, then a run); the sum code read between them writes an output the PLACING never saved, so the write sends nothing (:431-433 registers the saved ports alone — NSP-020 §6.6 piece 5)

name: a throw ends the run: what it wrote before stays, and the next run runs
because: javascript.ts :492-508 (caught, logged, not on the wire)

name: a throw in a signal's function, and a thrown string: the next pulse runs it again
a throw of null, in a run or a signal's function, ends that call and the next one runs (row C148)
because: javascript.ts :492-508, :520-537 — every catch read the thrown value's prototype and threw before the scheduled flag cleared, so the code never ran again; fixed in P109 ISL-051

name: code that does not compile, or throws while read, leaves the code before running — after its destroy
empty code is ignored: the code before keeps running
script(): a changed handler gets the new and the old value, methods and setOutputs are on this, a signal from signals
script() with an input at the placing: setup runs before the first run
because: javascript.ts :422-440 (setup asked for before the run; the held input replayed after)

name: the Node object: OnInit, Setters for what arrived, OnInputsChanged, a Signals function, and a top-level let that starts again when the code is read again
this.sendSignalOnOutput and this.flagOutputDirty; a write to a name that is no output is kept on outputs
no code: values wait, and arrive when code is first read — out through the ports the placing saved (the written lists)
because: javascript.ts :651-659 (held before the first read), :433-440 (handed over after it), :431-433 (the SAVED ports registered at the read) — a placing with no code saves only its lists, and the input picker has no Signal (:735-762), so a signal cannot wait here: scenario 'a signal before the first read' grades that on a placing with code (NSP-020 §6.6 piece 5)
